title: Adjust a rear drum brake to a light drag with a brake spoon through the backing-plate hole, feeling the drag by hand
instruction: Adjust the rear brake with the brake spoon so that the drum turns by hand with a light drag. Do not over-tighten it and do not drop the spoon. Take the spoon out of the adjusting hole and let go of the drum when you are done.
context: Adjusting drum brake shoes with a brake spoon through the backing-plate hole is routine work for automotive service technicians and mechanics (SOC 49-3023, about 825,800 jobs in 2025, BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook): rear drum brakes are on many cars and light trucks, and after new shoes or a drum service the shoes must be set before the car is driven. The usual way (not given to the robot), as in the Chrysler factory procedure: put the spoon through the hole onto the star wheel, which cannot be seen, and lever it upward a notch at a time to expand the shoes until a slight drag is felt when the drum is turned. Too far cannot be undone with the spoon alone (the self-adjuster pawl holds the wheel; backing off needs a second tool to hold the lever off). Factory procedures then back off a set amount; this task ends at light drag.
setup: Positions are measured forward from the line joining the two arm bases (61 cm apart), left (+) or right (-) of their midline as seen from behind the robot, and up from the table top. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot. Brake: a GM-pattern 9-1/2 x 2 in duo-servo rear drum brake on its backing plate (black, 10.7 in across) and stub axle, on a blue hub stand (knuckle, post and base plate) standing on the table. Axle: 34.0 cm forward, 2.0 cm right, 21.0 cm up, running left-right; the drum (ID 9.5 in, depth 2.61 in) and its face toward the left, the backing plate's back face 6.5 cm right of the midline. Wheel studs: five 1/2-20, 1.5 in long, on a 4-3/4 in circle; one is level with the axle on the robot's side (28.0 cm forward). Adjusting hole: 1/2 x 3/4 in, in the backing plate 9.0 cm below the axle, its lower edge 2 mm below the star wheel's axis; its rubber cover lies on the table at 20 cm forward, 6 cm right. Star wheel (hidden): 24 teeth, 0.797 in across, its axis pointing forward (the adjusting screw lies across the bottom of the brake), its teeth 6 mm inside the plate behind the hole; on this brake its teeth moved upward through the hole expand the shoes. The shoes are backed off: the linings touch the drum after about 6 notches. Spoon: a 9 in brake adjusting spoon (red-dipped 12 cm grip, 1/2 in square, black 8 mm blade ending in a 1 mm edge) lying flat on two wooden rests, along the left-right line, tip toward the brake: 22.0 cm forward, tip 9.5 cm right of the midline, 6.6 cm up (its centre line).
scoring: Score 0 for the whole trial, from the moment it happens, whatever was reached before or after: over-adjusted (the drum's turning torque above 1.0 N m at any step, drum locked included; the self-adjuster pawl stops the spoon undoing it), or the spoon dropped (on the bench or floor). Otherwise the highest level reached: 0.25 the spoon's tip through the hole and in among the star wheel's teeth (inside the 10.1 mm tooth-tip circle, on the 6 mm face); 0.5 also the wheel turned 5 notches or more the expanding way; 0.75 the drum's turning torque within 0.3-1.0 N m (light drag); 1.0 the after-release check passed: it starts once the tip is 1 cm or more out of the hole and every finger pad has stayed 3 cm or more from the brake for 1 s without a break (the count restarts if one comes closer); then a torque about the axle ramped 0 to 1.2 N m over 3 s must turn the drum 2 degrees at a torque within 0.3-1.0 N m. Real trial: notches counted by the pawl's clicks; turning torque with a spring scale hooked on a stud 60.3 mm from the axle and pulled square (5.0-16.6 N); a scribed depth line on the blade; the video for a dropped spoon.
run_limit: 2,000 steps (100 s at 20 Hz); the scripted demo finishes in 1,481 steps (74 s)
reset_notes: Hold the self-adjuster lever off the star wheel with a screwdriver through the hole and back the wheel off with the spoon until the linings clear (count the notches back to the documented start, about 6 before drag), check the drum turns freely, turn the drum so one stud is level with the axle on the robot's side, lay the spoon on its rests and the hole's cover on the table. About 3 minutes.
fidelity: PhysX 480 Hz, i2rt gains. Plate with a real 1/2 x 3/4 in hole; star wheel 20 mm, its hub a collider. Tooth rule: tip in among the teeth, the wheel follows its angle (expanding only), 0.03 N m pushed back on the tip. Pawl rule: a click per 15 deg, holds backward. Drag rule: drum Coulomb drive, 0.15 N m hub + 0.25 N m per notch past lining contact (6.2 notches; inferred). 9 in spoon, free body. Torque check applied in sim. Details in README.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (arms move near their bases, never reach spoon or drum); demo (cameras and joint states only): 1.0; control (24 strokes, drag never felt): 0.0 (over-adjusted)
